Findings.Title: A second lease sweep can requeue a newer or completed HV request
Findings.Defect: ExpireHvRunLeasesCommand selects active expired runs before its per-run transaction, but inside that transaction rechecks only expiry. It does not recheck active status or whether this is still the request current attempt, and abandonment does not release or clear the expired lease. HvRetryDecision then changes the request without a terminal-state guard.
Findings.Evidence: Contract counterexample, not an execution of proposed code: sweep A and sweep B both select expired run R. A abandons R and queues its request. A new run R2 is claimed and may complete. B enters its transaction for R: the old expiry still has passed, so B abandons R again and applies HvRetryDecision to the now Running or Completed request. It becomes Queued or Failed, possibly releasing turns and emitting a false terminal notification. The artifact-worker sweep at 1747 explicitly rechecks active state and refuses an accepted request; that round 2 repair was not propagated to the HV sweep. SerializableWrite cannot repair a stale candidate unless its delegate revalidates the state.
Findings.ChangeToPass: Make expiry an idempotent, guarded transition in the transaction: re-read active run status, current ownership/attempt and request eligibility, and skip an already settled or superseded candidate. Ensure terminal requests cannot be revived. Cover two sweepers with an intervening claim and an intervening successful finalization, with named tests in FR/TR/TEST-MCP-HVPIPE-007 at H3 and the finalization case at H7; update the policy, unit, caller diagrams and phase bindings.

Findings.Title: A probe consumes evidence before its read audit is durable
Findings.Defect: RecordRead enlists its ledger row in the caller transaction when one exists. CloseHvRunOutputCommand then consumes and verifies the probe chunks inside that same transaction. The read audit is only committed after the consumption that it is required to precede.
Findings.Evidence: The AuditLedgerGuard diagram explicitly says read recorded with the caller commit. A crash, transaction conflict or commit failure after ReadinessProbeVerdict consumes bytes rolls back the read row. The evidence was consumed but no durable read record remains. Checking that DataAuditLogs is writable and staging a row are not a durable audit of that access. This contradicts S-29, R-19 and I-13 and leaves the internal-reader part of R2-F08 unresolved.
Findings.ChangeToPass: Specify a durable audit boundary that succeeds before any evidence byte is consumed and survives a subsequent caller rollback. Preserve fencing and probe-state concurrency without claiming an uncommitted row is durable. Add named probe-read rollback/crash/commit-failure cases to the existing audit requirement, with the mock gate first and H3 binding, and propagate the boundary to every internal reader and its caller outcome.

Findings.Title: An idempotent submission replay returns output without an evidence-read audit

Findings.Evidence: Replay an accepted submission after the reviewer has emitted a chunk. The specified same-input path goes directly from IdempotentCreate to 200 HvRequestResult. Returning its lastOutput must read/decompress stored evidence, yet no read row is required and the Submit error list describes evidence_corrupt only for the original admission round trip. A reachable public read therefore bypasses the new audited boundary.
Findings.ChangeToPass: Define one consistent replay projection: either use the canonical audited current-request projection, including corruption and audit-refusal outcomes, or explicitly define a distinct output-free submission response everywhere it is used. Add a named replay-after-output test, ledger-refusal test and corrupt-output case at a phase with stored run output and the relevant surface. Update DTOs, Submit activity/sequence, reader/component user lists, FR/TR/TEST and phase ownership.

Findings.Title: The artifact completion contract cannot carry required execution metadata and leaves terminal fields unwritten
Findings.Defect: HostileReviewAttemptOutcome contains executionId but no actual model, effort, agent/source, template/version, start/end, or optional token/runtime metadata. CompleteHostileReviewAttemptCommand is nevertheless told to write the execution row with its metadata, without a source or parameter carrying it. Attempt.ExecutionId is written only on the first renewal, so a process that exits before RenewalInterval has no specified writer for that relationship. EndedUtc is set only on success, not on failure or cancellation.
Findings.Evidence: The host diagram permits reviewer exited before any renewal timer. Complete accepts a Claimed attempt, writes an execution row from Outcome.executionId, and finishes without setting the attempt ExecutionId. The existing execution entity requires ReviewerAgent, Model and Effort and holds SourceSurface, PromptTemplateId, PromptVersion, StartedUtc, EndedUtc and token counts. Those values cannot be reconstructed faithfully from the declared completion DTO, especially actual-versus-configured identity. The stored requirement demands execution metadata and omission with a diagnostic when optional metrics are unavailable. A sentence promising metadata does not define the missing data flow.
Findings.ChangeToPass: Define a canonical normalized execution-metadata contract and its producer, carrying actual identity and the required timing/template fields plus optional metrics or explicit unavailability diagnostics. Define writers for ExecutionId and every terminal timestamp on fast success, failure, cancellation, expiry and no-launch outcomes, preserving the no-raw-artifact rule. Add named fast-exit and metadata/missing-metric cases through TEST-MCP-HOSTILEREVIEW-003 in H0 after approval and bind them in H3. Reconcile all units, DTOs and B.9.
